title: UN Commission of Inquiry says energy grid attacks may amount to crimes against humanity
body:
On 16 March 2023 the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine, chaired by Erik Mose, said that Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy-related infrastructure since 10 October 2022 may amount to crimes against humanity. UN News reported that the attacks had left millions of people without power in freezing temperatures.

The Commission also reported that Russian authorities had used torture in a systematic manner in the areas it examined. Commissioner Pablo de Greiff pointed to elements of planning and resources behind the practice, which led the Commission to say that Russian authorities may have committed crimes against humanity, and it recommended further investigation into whether these acts followed a specific policy.

The Commission said it had covered nine Ukrainian regions, visited 56 towns and interviewed close to 600 witnesses. Victims of sexual violence ranged in age from four to 82 years. The Commission found two incidents committed by Ukrainian forces that qualified as war crimes, both involving Russian prisoners of war. Its first report, in October 2022, had found that Russia had committed war crimes in the Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kharkiv and Sumy regions.
